newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa denies putting stamp on new group.
newsitem.headline: Axa denies putting stamp on new group.

text.p: French insurance company Axa on Monday denied a newspaper report that it was seeking to put its stamp on the planned new corporate giant to be born of its merger with rival UAP.
"We have always said this will be a merger of equals," said an Axa spokeswoman. "The future (structure) will reflect that. There is no struggle under way. Everything is proceeding smoothly."
She said that the new executive structure should be announced "fairly quickly" after the closure of Axa's share swap offer for Union des Assurances de Paris on December 18.
The newspaper Le Monde said the new executive lineup would be announced at the end of the week and that intense jockeying was under way for the top spots in the new organisation.
The newspaper said UAP chairman Jacques Friedmann wanted UAP staff and Axa to be represented equally while Axa chairman Claude Bebear wanted to "to impose the Axa stamp on all levels".
The daily said "continuous and strained negotiations" had been going on for two weeks.
Axa and Union des Assurances de Paris announced last month plans to merge in a deal initially valued at 40 billion francs ($7.63 billion).
The agreement will create the world's second largest insurer with annual premium income of more than 300 billion francs.

While Axa insisted when the deal was announced that it represented "a friendly operation between equals", insurance analysts have said they believe there is little doubt that highly profitable Axa would dominate its larger, formerly state-owned partner UAP which only recently returned to profit.

Analysts have said it may be hard to merge the corporate cultures of the two insurers. UAP has a reputation for being stodgy and bureaucratic, a legacy of its state ownership, while Axa is known for being much more profit-driven.
The two companies have already announced that the new group, which still has to be named, will have a two tier-management structure.

Bebear is to chair an operating committee, making him effective chief executive officer, while Friedmann will have a position similar to president, heading a supervisory and strategic committee. ($1=5.243 French Franc)
